stories.summary: Add Full Video Player to SwingDetailScreen

details.user_story: As a User, I want to watch my swing video with skeleton overlay from the swing detail screen so that I can review my analysis without navigating away.
details.context:
Currently, SwingDetailScreen only shows the video filename and server path. Users can edit title/notes and view analysis data, but cannot watch the video.

The main RecordScreen has a full video player with:
- VideoView component with expo-video
- Skeleton overlay synchronized with playback
- Bat trail visualization
- Frame-by-frame scrubbing (DM-59)
- Fullscreen mode

We should add similar functionality to SwingDetailScreen so users can review their swings.
acceptance_criteria: Add VideoView component to SwingDetailScreen
Display video with skeleton overlay from analysis data
Show bat trail if available
Include frame-by-frame scrubbing controls (from DM-59)
Support fullscreen mode
Video plays automatically when screen loads
Skeleton overlay syncs with video playback
Works with both local and remote video URLs
technical_details: - Set up timeUpdate listener for frame sync
- Add video player above title/notes section
- Handle video_url (may need to construct full URL)
- Check if video_url is relative path
- SwingDetailScreen.js - Add video player and controls
- May need to update backend to serve videos via HTTP
edge_cases: Video URL is local file path - construct full HTTP URL
Video file deleted from server - show error message
Large video file - show loading indicator
No skeletal data - show video without overlay
Video fails to load - show error with retry button
Screen orientation changes - maintain playback position

details.user_story: As a Developer, I want videos to be accessible via HTTP URLs so that the mobile app can stream them directly.
details.context:
Currently, video_url in the database stores local file paths like `/backend/uploads/video.mp4`. These cannot be opened by the mobile app using Linking.openURL() or streamed in a video player.

We need to either:
1. Serve videos via a FastAPI static file endpoint
2. Upload videos to cloud storage (S3, Supabase Storage) and store HTTP URLs

Option 1 is simpler for MVP, Option 2 is better for production scale.
acceptance_criteria: Videos accessible via HTTP URL (e.g., https://backend.com/videos/{filename})
Support video streaming (range requests for seeking)
CORS headers configured for mobile app access
Proper content-type headers (video/mp4)
Authentication/authorization for video access (optional)
Update video_url in database to store full HTTP URLs
technical_details: Option 1: FastAPI Static Files (Recommended for MVP)
- Use Supabase Storage or AWS S3
- Store public URL in video_url column
1. Add static file mount for /videos endpoint
2. Update upload endpoint to store full URL
3. Add CORS headers for video streaming
4. Test range requests for video seeking
- Update existing video_url records to full URLs
- Script: `UPDATE swings SET video_url = CONCAT('https://backend.com', video_url)`
edge_cases: Large video files - ensure streaming works (range requests)
Concurrent video access - check server capacity
Video file permissions - ensure readable by web server
HTTPS required for mobile apps - configure SSL
Video deleted but URL still in DB - return 404 gracefully

details.user_story: As a User, I want my videos compressed before upload so that uploads are faster and don't crash the AI service.
details.context:
DM-29 added video compression infrastructure, but actual compression is disabled in Expo Go due to native module limitations.

Current State:
- VideoCompressionService exists with proper API
- UI for compression progress implemented
- Service currently skips compression and returns original file
- Works in Expo Go for development

Target State:
- Compress videos to 720p @ 2.5 Mbps before upload
- Reduce file sizes from 50-100MB to 10-20MB
- Prevent AI service crashes (512MB RAM limit)
- Improve upload speed and data usage

This is a duplicate of DM-58, created earlier.
acceptance_criteria: Replace stub compression in VideoCompressionService with real FFmpeg or native compression
Compress videos to 720p (1280px width) with 2.5 Mbps bitrate
Skip compression for files already < 10MB
Show accurate progress during compression (0-100%)
Handle compression failures gracefully (fallback to original)
Test on iOS and Android physical devices
Verify compressed videos upload successfully
Verify AI service processes compressed videos without crashes
Measure compression time (target: < 10s for 30s video)
Measure file size reduction (target: 70-80% reduction)
technical_details: See DM-58 for full implementation details
This ticket is a duplicate - close in favor of DM-58
